# Recorded simulation fault investigation

**Environment:** Educational ladder interpreter; virtual voltage nodes, no physical meter or hardware. These readings were generated by running the simulator, not by measuring physical hardware.

**Reported symptom:** Start Fill is requested with an empty vessel, but no water enters and K1 / Q0.0 stays off.

**Known-good conditions:** PS1 is 24 V; STOP_OK and OL_OK are true; the high-level contact should be closed below 40 L.

**Diagnostic path:**

1. Confirm the symptom at the tank and fill output image.
2. Inspect I0.3 / HIGH_OK: false despite an empty tank.
3. Compare the virtual voltage before wire 104 with the PLC end, referenced to 0 V.
4. Find 24 V upstream and 0 V at X1:04. R05 and R06 cannot pass their HIGH_OK contacts.
5. Restore the simulated open conductor. Verify that HIGH_OK returns true without an automatic fill restart.
6. Apply a fresh Start edge, fill to the high switch, then drain to the low switch. Verify that outputs turn off at both endpoints.

**Root cause:** Open conductor 104 between the NC high-level contact and PLC I0.3 / X1:04. This is a known injected open-circuit fault; the exercise does not claim that these readings alone exclude every possible real-world input-module fault.

**Correction:** Restore the simulated conductor, verify input recovery, then issue a fresh start.

| Captured checkpoint | Upstream V | PLC input V | HIGH_OK | FILL_OUT | Tank L |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Healthy empty vessel, before start | 24 | 24 | 1 | 0 | 0.0 |
| Fault injected: open wire 104 at X1:04; fill start attempted | 24 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.0 |
| Wire restored: input recovers; no automatic restart | 24 | 24 | 1 | 0 | 0.0 |
| Fresh start after repair: fill output energizes | 24 | 24 | 1 | 1 | 0.2 |
| Retest: high-level permissive opens and stops filling | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 40.0 |
| Retest: drain completes and pump stops at low level | 24 | 24 | 1 | 0 | 0.0 |

**Result: PASS.** Full unrounded circuit values and simulated timestamps are in [open-wire-diagnosis.json](open-wire-diagnosis.json).

## Distinguishing a normal stop from a wiring fault

At 40 L, the high-level NC contact opens normally: both its output and the PLC end read 0 V. With the injected open wire below 40 L, the contact output is 24 V but the PLC end is 0 V. The simulator assumes a pull-down at the input so the open node is defined as 0 V.

## Scope

No physical PLC, vendor engineering environment, panel wiring, commissioning or meter work was performed. This is an educational interpreter supporting true/false contacts, parallel branches, ordinary coils, rising-edge blocks and TON timers. It does not establish vendor PLC programming experience.
